final_decisions: v1 trust model is server-side envelope encryption. Client-side zero-knowledge encryption is not mixed into v1 and would require a separate major architecture.
Each secret version receives a fresh random 256-bit DEK and XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD nonce. DEKs are wrapped by a versioned KEK provider key.
OpenBao is the reference production KEK/Transit provider. A local development provider exists only for non-production tests and is clearly marked unsafe for production.
AAD is canonical and versioned: vault_id, secret_id, secret_version, owner_scope, classification, algorithm_version. AAD mismatch is integrity failure.
Plaintext is never persisted, queued, cached, indexed, traced or logged. Sensitive request fields are excluded at the telemetry instrumentation boundary.
Passkey/WebAuthn + MFA/step-up is required for reveal/export/key rotation/member privilege changes according to policy.
Recovery restores account control, not lost cryptographic roots. If the KEK provider root is irrecoverably lost, ciphertext is intentionally unrecoverable.
Audit events are hash-chained; periodic Merkle/checkpoint roots are signed through OpenBao Transit and stored separately for tamper evidence.
Algorithm agility is carried in KeyEnvelope v1; no custom primitives are implemented.

data_ownership.PostgreSQL: ciphertext envelopes, metadata, policy, audit records
data_ownership.OpenBao: KEK/signing root operations, never DB plaintext
